feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It is well written overall, but it is slightly repetitive and could be sharper on measurable outcomes, prioritization, and consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director, which strengthens credibility.  
- Strong domain positioning: digital platforms, governance, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are presented as a coherent leadership profile.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap heavily and dilute impact. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond scope metrics: e.g., efficiency gains, engagement growth, adoption improvements, cost savings, or campaign results.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” mixed list punctuation, and inconsistent capitalization emphasis in “Coleman DAVIS.” No major misspellings found; grammar is strong overall. Minor stylistic tweak: “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler in Education.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more specific: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years guiding web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Add scale/relevance from recent roles: reference enterprise websites, large publisher groups, or audience volume (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).
- Replace “Leads” with a results-oriented phrase such as “delivers” or “oversees” to sound less generic and more evidence-based.
- Consider trimming “multimedia production” or “AI-enabled user experiences” unless those are key targets for the roles you’re applying to.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader,” “web modernization,” “governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled…” repeat language already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and skills sections.
- “Public-sector communications” is reinforced throughout work experience, so the intro can focus more on differentiation and scale.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made slightly more distinctive, and aligned in style.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace broad items with sharper, higher-value terms: “Cross-channel communications operations” or “Digital operations leadership” may read stronger than “Multi-channel communications operations.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, cut one lower-priority item and keep the most differentiating strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and public-sector communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats the header and recent projects.
- Several items duplicate Topline Skills almost verbatim, especially governance, analytics, workflow automation, and multimedia.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make the footer feel more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/led X using Y to achieve Z.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “improve discovery” or “designed for continued campaign growth” with measurable or clearer outcomes if available.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “Drupal 10,” and spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite closely overlap with the current freelance role; consider framing them as named examples rather than restating duties.
- Advocacy Video Series repeats NACo video accomplishments; shorten or swap for a less-covered project if space is tight.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic/technical scope, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes and distinguish it from the NACo entries by emphasizing consulting impact, enterprise improvement, and AI/search leadership.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, campaign delivery, and web modernization.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics processes to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Recast the AI item as a flagship achievement: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery experience.” Add metrics if possible: pages improved, teams supported, launch dates, traffic, time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “digital strategy” strongly overlap with the Director of Digital Media role; keep this entry focused on consulting/advisory and new initiatives.
- The microsite and AI search bullets duplicate Recent Projects; keep one concise here and let the project section carry detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization win and keep the metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-oriented: add audience growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets to emphasize transformation: built first in-house broadcast studio; expanded analytics stack (GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery); formalized governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video leadership also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support work than a step-up into leadership. Tighten it around scope, coordination, and channel ownership, with any metrics you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show level and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with ownership: “Built more consistent editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the earlier Digital Media Manager / Producer role; distinguish this entry by emphasizing scale or formalization.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most current strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations systems
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider adding one higher-impact qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “enterprise web modernization” or “AI-enabled content discovery,” if you want this section to reflect current positioning.
- Keep wording parallel: use either all noun phrases or all “X leadership/strategy” constructions.
- Remove filler like “focused” where a stronger term such as “centered” or “driven” is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to modernization and delivery rather than listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older items unless job-relevant; keep the strongest recent signals: Drupal, CMS modernization, API/workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Remove “jQuery” here; it dates the profile and is better left to Technical + IT if needed.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Large-scale Drupal platform delivery” to echo recent 10,000+ page migration work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; avoid repeating WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable, and coding languages in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; keep it in one place only unless it is a signature differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize strategic analytics capability, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Analytics infrastructure & performance optimization”
- Use grouped phrasing for concision: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic items with stronger business language: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “leadership reporting,” “SEO and conversion/performance analysis”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave full platform inventory to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it’s currently generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and technical production strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Production, Studio & Live Event Delivery
- Tighten and sharpen the list: Video production and post-production • Livestream and webcast production • PTZ camera and studio systems • Hybrid, virtual and on-site event delivery
- If accurate, add scale/complexity rather than generic terms: e.g., Multi-camera production, broadcast-quality studio operations, executive/internal stakeholder event support
- Keep wording outcome-oriented and operational, not tool-heavy, since tools already appear in “Technical + IT”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” and “Livestreaming” repeat content already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience; use broader phrasing like “live event delivery” or “studio systems” to add new value.
- Avoid repeating software here; Premiere Pro and related tools are already listed under “Multimedia & Creative Tools.”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. In Technical + IT, this should feel more implementation-focused and emphasize the strongest, most recent platform first.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine if Drupal remains first; consider adding versions/scope only if true, e.g. **Drupal 10, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**.
- Make it slightly more technical: **CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to actual work: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep this item platform-only; leave modernization, integrations, and AI/search to adjacent skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider trimming one list or differentiating this one as “platforms used” and the other as “capabilities.”
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms unless it supports a portfolio or project use case.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add specificity tied to recent work: front-end CMS implementation, tag deployment, serverless scripting, CI/CD support
- Consider a stronger version: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • GTM implementation • Cloudflare Workers (serverless scripts) • GitHub Actions (deployment automation)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact wording in both places.
- If this section stays as a list, don’t also claim the same tools in multiple project bullets unless tied to a concrete outcome.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tool coverage, but this item is currently just a software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it around automation/integration tools and move generic collaboration apps out unless they are central to workflow design.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Project Systems
- Rewrite as: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses for stronger signal: Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automations) • Jira/Asana/Trello (project workflow management)
- Consider ordering by relevance to recent work: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier first, then project systems

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack” and “Teams” read as general collaboration tools, not distinctive technical skills; they add little value here.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same language verbatim.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/operational context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email/engagement platform ownership, not just list vendor names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations, audience segmentation and campaign delivery**
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **…supporting high-volume member communications and recurring newsletter programs reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders**
- Keep platform names in order of strongest/recent relevance; if Dynamics 365 was only limited exposure, move it after Higher Logic or remove it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Newsletter operations” and “campaign delivery” already appear in work experience; only keep them here if phrased as platform capability, not role responsibility.
- Avoid adding “multi-channel communications” here; that’s already covered in Core Competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of use or business impact. Tighten it into a sharper category label and more outcome-oriented phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization Tools
- Rewrite as: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI • KPI reporting and dashboard development • SEO analysis • A/B testing
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting and dashboard development” for clearer value.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to impact in recent roles rather than listing more platforms here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping detail in only one place.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 Director role, so avoid repeating the same language verbatim.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, since strategy/leadership are already covered in the 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence to focus on execution: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate’s day-to-day work.”
- If possible, replace “high-impact digital content” with specifics tied to reach, frequency, or organizational value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this at a lighter, foundational level.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting NACo programs and policy initiatives.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead point and sharpen phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Condense the rest into one supporting clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and innovation/project coordination.
- Avoid broad “supported organizational programs and policy work” language if similar phrasing appears elsewhere; specify program, initiative, or output where possible.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets, so tighten it to tool proficiency and keep broader production strengths elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
- Rewrite as: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want to retain non-software skills, split them into a separate item: Livestream studio operations • Podcast production
- If space is tight, consider dropping Photoshop/Illustrator unless they are used regularly in recent roles; Premiere Pro and Audition are the strongest fit
